title.narrative: TRANSFORM

description.narrative: Ethiopia has implemented a range of initiatives to enhance agricultural productivity, including providing small-scale farmers with fertilizers, high-quality seeds, and training in improved farming techniques. However, soil health continues to decline, with widespread issues such as acidity, salinity, nutrient depletion, low organic matter, and erosion, signs of persistent land degradation that threaten the sustainability of agriculture. This deterioration not only reduces crop yields but also endangers the livelihoods of millions of farmers who rely on agriculture as their primary source of income. To address the productivity gap while conserving and restoring soil health, the TRANSFORM Program aims to actively engage small-scale farmers in the solutions. TRANSFORM will be implemented over four years, from 2025 to 2028, across three regions: Oromia, Amhara, and Central Ethiopia.TRANSFORM is structured around four key components: (i) customizing soil fertility extension services to empower farmer households and communities, (ii) building a vibrant sector for soil inputs to ensure that farmers have access to essential resources, (iii) strengthening linkages between research and extension through bottom-up, participatory farmer-led action research, which promotes innovative solutions tailored to local contexts, and (iv) fostering an enabling environment for soil health and fertility to encourage collaborative efforts among stakeholders. The Program is implemented by a consortium of partners, including the IFDC as the lead partner, along with Stichting Wageningen Research (SWR) - Wageningen Environmental Research (WENR), ISRIC – World Soil Information, the Environment and Coffee Forest Forum (ECFF), and SOS Sahel (Ethiopia) as the implementing partners. Together, these partners are committed to establishing sustainable soil health and fertility management practices to support a resilient agricultural landscape in Ethiopia.

General objective:- to see 65,000 ha of farmland converted to sustainable land use. - to enhance 100,000 small-scale food producers and their agro-ecological farmlands become more resilient to shocks- to achieve systemic uplift and transformation of local and multi-sectoral actors with strengthened knowledge and implementation capacity for soil fertility and health.Specific objectives:- to resile and empower small-scale farmers and communities to become stewards of their soils.- to establish a vibrant and functional soil input system through private sector- to implement inclusive, bottom-up, participatory approaches to soil health and fertility management - to adopt an integrated and holistic approach for coordinating soil health and fertility management.Expected Outcomes- Empowered Households: the integration of sustainable soil health and fertility management improves soil and crop productivity, increases household incomes, enhances food security, provides better livelihoods, and promotes sustainable use of soil resources.- Restored Farmlands: implementing integrated land management practices enhances soil health, increases biodiversity, and improves water management, ultimately resulting in more sustainable agricultural systems and greater resilience to climate change.- Enhanced Community Knowledge: The enhanced knowledge and skills of local communities and multi-sectoral actors in sustainable soil health management promote the adoption of sustainable soil health and fertility practices, increase resilience to environmental and economic challenges, and foster a brighter future for generations to come.Expected outputs:- Sustainable soil health and fertility management practices integrated and empowered 100,000 households, with 30% participation from women and 30% from youth.- Integrated land management practices implemented across 128 kebeles and 128 watersheds and sustainably restored 65,000 hectares of farmland.- Capacity (knowledge and skills) of local and multi-sectoral actors for implementing sustainable soil fertility and health practices enhanced through targeted training, practical demonstrations, and partnerships, leading to improved agricultural productivity and community resilience.- National and regional soil health and fertility platforms established and institutionalized that integrate a holistic approach, fostering coordination and alignment among soil actors and stakeholders at all levels and creating an enabling environment for informed policy decisions.
